quote: Commerce One shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Corio and its Customers from any and all damages, liabilities, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) incurred by Corio or its Customers arising out of any claim that the Software infringes any patent, copyright, trademark or trade right secret of a third party
rationale: Commerce One gives a defence-and-indemnity for third-party IP infringement covering us and our Customers, with the usual notice/control/cooperation procedure, procure-modify-refund remedies and only standard exclusions (out-of-documentation use, third-party modification), and it sits outside the liability cap; we owe no reciprocal indemnity. This meets the fallback (and beyond, being uncapped); it does not extend to breach of law, data breach or gross negligence, which we note but do not flag.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot transfer ownership of interface code we create to Commerce One merely because Commerce One supports it on an ongoing basis; we own what we build and pay for. Commerce One's pre-existing IP and the Software remain its own.

ops.newText: shall be owned by Corio, including
ops.oldText: shall be owned by Corio, unless such Developments are supported on an ongoing basis by Commerce One in which case Commerce One will retain all ownership rights, including

proposal.summary: Delete reversion of Corio-created Developments to Commerce One where Commerce One provides ongoing support

quote: shall be owned by Corio, unless such Developments are supported on an ongoing basis by Commerce One in which case Commerce One will retain all ownership rights, including
rationale: Section 13.5 gives us ownership of the interface code we create, but then hands ownership of those same Developments to Commerce One whenever it supports them on an ongoing basis — an effective assignment of our IP to the Vendor, which is walk-away territory. We delete the reversion; Commerce One's pre-existing IP and the Software itself remain untouched. We also note the agreement has no Customer Data ownership provision.
ruleTitle: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position is a mutual cap of the 12 months' fees paid or payable (not a per-transaction slice, which could be a trivial amount) with confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud, alongside indemnification, sitting outside the cap.

ops.newText: THE TOTAL AMOUNT PAID OR PAYABLE BY CORIO HEREUNDER DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE LIABILITY.
ops.oldText: THE TOTAL AMOUNT ACTUALLY PAID BY CORIO HEREUNDER FOR THE TRANSACTION WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES TO DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO THE FILING OF THE CAUSE OF ACTION TO WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES.

ops.text: The limitations set forth in this Section 9 shall not apply to either party's breach of its confidentiality obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, or Corio's obligation to pay fees due under this Agreement.

proposal.summary: Cap based on 12 months' fees (not per-transaction) and add confidentiality/gross negligence/wilful misconduct carve-outs

quote: EXCEPT FOR LIABILITY ARISING UNDER SECTION 8 OF THIS AGREEMENT, IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT OR THE USE OR PERFORMANCE OF THE SOFTWARE EXCEED THE TOTAL AMOUNT ACTUALLY PAID BY CORIO HEREUNDER FOR THE TRANSACTION WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES TO DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO THE FILING OF THE CAUSE OF ACTION TO WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES.
rationale: The cap is mutual and indemnification (Section 8) sits outside it, but the cap base is only amounts paid "for the transaction which the liability relates to" in the preceding 12 months — a per-transaction slice that can fall far below 6 months' fees — and the only carve-out is indemnification, with nothing for confidentiality, gross negligence or wilful misconduct. That fails the fallback on both material terms, so we reset the base to 12 months' fees paid or payable and add the standard carve-out sentence.
ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs

quote: Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party shall have the right to assign this Agreement in connection with the merger or acquisition of such party or the sale of all or substantially all of its assets related to this Agreement without such consent, except in the case where such transaction involves a direct competitor of the other party where consent of the other party will be required.
rationale: Assignment is mutual with an M&A/asset-sale carve-out for us, and no Commerce One termination or re-pricing right is triggered by our change of control, which meets the fallback. We note two sub-optimal points: the consent standard is not qualified as "not unreasonably withheld", and consent is still required where the acquirer is a direct competitor of Commerce One.

quote: Under no circumstances shall Commerce One contact Corio Customers regarding a non-ASP license sale, unless requested to do so by Corio.
rationale: No exclusivity, sole-supplier or requirements obligation binds us; the licences are expressly nonexclusive and we remain free to source competing software. The only channel restraint runs against Commerce One (no direct approaches to our Customers, referrals back to us), which benefits us and we leave intact.

quote: If either party materially breaches any term or condition of this Agreement and fails to cure such breach within-thirty (30) days after receiving written notice of the breach, the nonbreaching party may terminate this Agreement on written notice at any time following the end of such-thirty (30) day period.
rationale: There are no liquidated damages, penalties, shortfall charges or early-termination fees payable by us; post-termination payments are limited to fees for continued Customer use and maintenance we choose to keep. Nothing to redline.
ruleTitle: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer

quote: Commerce One hereby grants to Corio a fee-bearing, perpetual and irrevocable, nonexclusive, nontransferable (except in accordance with Section 14.1 of this Agreement), right and license in the Territory
rationale: The hosting licence is perpetual and irrevocable, transferable to a successor via Section 14.1, permits unlimited sublicensing to our Customers, and Section 14.8 expressly allows us to subcontract portions of the Corio Services — so contractors and successors are covered and the walk-away risks (revocable at will, no path for third parties) are absent. Affiliates are not expressly named, which we note rather than flag.

quote: "CORIO MARKET SEGMENT" means those customers with annual sales revenues of less than $1,000,000,000.
rationale: There is no covenant restricting the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build; the only scope limits are licence-scope ones (the Corio Market Segment and the North America Territory), and they come with the right to retain Customers that grow past the threshold and an expansion mechanism under Section 2.10 in which consent cannot be unreasonably withheld. Worth noting as commercial scope, not a restrictive covenant.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We do not commit to a five-year term without an exit; we need a convenience right on 30 days' notice with a refund of prepaid fees (fallback: 60–90 days' notice). Commerce One gains no convenience right.

ops.text: 11.1A Termination for Convenience. Corio may terminate this Agreement for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Commerce One, in which case Commerce One shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination. Commerce One shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience.

proposal.summary: Add Corio termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund

quote: The term of this Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and shall continue in full force and effect for an initial period of five (5) years.
rationale: Termination is available only for uncured material breach or insolvency; neither party may terminate for convenience during a five-year committed term, which is the walk-away case of no Customer convenience right in a multi-year term. We add a 30 days' notice convenience right with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees (fallback 60–90 days) and leave Commerce One without any convenience right.

quote: Such inspections may be made no more than once each calendar year, at reasonable times and upon reasonable notice. Commerce One shall bear all costs and expenses of such inspection.
rationale: Audits are limited to once a calendar year by an independent CPA reasonably acceptable to us, at Commerce One's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and are confined to books and records with no access to our systems — at or above our preferred position. Notice is "reasonable" rather than a fixed 30 days, which we note only.

quote: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of California, USA, excluding conflict of laws provisions and excluding the 1980 United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods. Any disputes arising out of this Agreement shall be resolved by binding arbitration in accordance with the then-current commercial arbitration rules of the American Arbitration Association ("RULES").
rationale: California law with a single-arbitrator AAA arbitration seated in San Francisco County and judgment enforceable in the California courts sits within the fallback (California law and forum); the seat is domestic, so there is no foreign-arbitration walk-away issue. We note only that we would prefer courts over mandatory arbitration.

The pricing exhibit and the body of the agreement contain no most-favoured-nation or price-matching obligation in either direction, so nothing obliges us to extend Commerce One terms given to third parties. No redline needed.

quote: Corio to pay Commerce One [*] of all Application Management Revenue from Corio Customers for use of Commerce One Software or MarketSite.net Service Access subject to the following limitations.
rationale: Fees are usage- and revenue-based (licence fees, annual maintenance, revenue share on actual Customer revenue, implementation on time and materials with a cap); there is no minimum purchase, take-or-pay or shortfall payment binding us. The "minimum limitation of 40 Authorized Software Users per Customer" is a revenue-share calculation threshold, not a purchase commitment.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

quote: The parties are independent contractors with respect to each other.
rationale: There is no non-solicitation or no-hire covenant anywhere in the agreement (searches for "solicit", "employ", "induce" return nothing), even though Commerce One personnel work alongside ours under Section 13. Nothing restricts our hiring, so no redline.

quote: Thereafter, this Agreement shall automatically renew for subsequent one (1) year periods unless either party provides the other party with written notification at least thirty (30) days prior to the expiration of the initial five (5) year term or any one (1) year renewal thereof of its intention to terminate this Agreement.
rationale: Renewals are 12 months with a 30-day non-renewal window exercisable by either party, which meets our preferred position on term length and notice. There is no Vendor renewal reminder and no cap on renewal price uplift (fees for years 2-5 and beyond are set in Exhibit B), which we note rather than flag.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We need an orderly exit: up to six months of transition assistance and return of our and our Customers' data in machine-readable form within 30 days (fallback: 90 days' assistance). This complements, and does not cut back, the survival rights in Section 11.3.

ops.text: 11.4 Transition Assistance and Data Return. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Commerce One shall (a) at Corio's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Commerce One's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of Corio's request, return to Corio all data of Corio and its Customers in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete such data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

proposal.summary: Insert transition assistance and data return obligations on termination

quote: Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement, each party shall otherwise return or destroy any Confidential Information of the other party provided, however, Corio may retain any Confidential Information necessary for Corio to continue supporting it's then-existing Customers.
rationale: Section 11.3 preserves our licence and Commerce One's maintenance obligations for existing Customers, but there is no transition-assistance obligation and no requirement to return or export the data Commerce One holds through the MarketSite.net Service in a machine-readable format. We insert a new Section 11.4 providing up to six months' assistance at then-current rates and 30-day data return with certified deletion (fallback: 90 days' assistance).
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

proposal.comment: [Playbook] A 60-day warranty that also expires on a fixed calendar date is below our floor of 90 days for software; we ask for 12 months, and would accept 90 days from acceptance as a fallback. The existing correction/replacement/refund remedy is unchanged.

ops.newText: for a period of twelve (12) months from the Effective Date (the "Warranty Period")
ops.oldText: for a period of sixty (60) days from the Effective Date, but in no event not later than December 31, 1999 (the "Warranty Period")

proposal.summary: Extend warranty period to 12 months and delete the fixed 31 December 1999 cut-off

quote: for a period of sixty (60) days from the Effective Date, but in no event not later than December 31, 1999 (the "Warranty Period")
rationale: The conformance warranty and remedies (correction, replacement, or termination with refund of prepaid fees) are sound, but the period is only 60 days from the Effective Date and is additionally cut off by a fixed calendar date, which is below our 90-day software floor and could leave almost no coverage. We extend the period to 12 months and delete the hard cut-off; 90 days is our fallback.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Vendors whose personnel work alongside ours and whose service handles transaction data should carry standard cover: CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M and cyber USD 5M (fallback: E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M). Subsequent subsections to be renumbered.

ops.text: 14.10 Insurance. Commerce One shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Commerce One processes data of Corio or its Customers, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Commerce One shall provide certificates of insurance to Corio on request.

proposal.summary: Insert a Vendor insurance covenant in Section 14

quote: 14.9 Bankruptcy. The parties hereto agree that Corio, as a licensee of Commerce One's intellectual property, shall be afforded all of the protections afforded to a licensee under Section 365(n) of the United States Bankruptcy Code
rationale: The agreement contains no insurance covenant at all, even though Commerce One hosts the MarketSite.net Service used by our Customers and supplies operations, consulting and engineering personnel who work with our teams. We insert a short Section 14 insurance paragraph (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M, certificates on request), with E&O 1M / cyber 2M as our fallback.
